Oct 17 : Inter Milan came from a goal down to beat Bologna 3-1 in Serie A on Saturday, maintaining their unbeaten start and going two points clear at the top. Inter, who suffered a shock home loss to Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday, went behind in the 10th minute to a goal from Tommaso Pobega but equalised through Marcus Thuram against the run of play just before halftime. Second-half goals from Carlos Augusto and Ange-Yoan Bonny helped secure the win that lifted them to 19 points with their sixth victory in seven league matches. Cristian Chivu's side are two points ahead of AS Roma, 2-0 winners over visitors Genoa thanks to second-half goals from Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli.

Oct 17 : Ireland's Billy Loughnane was crowned Britain's champion jockey at Ascot on Saturday, making the 20-year-old the youngest rider to win the title in more than a century.  Loughnane beat fellow Irishman and five-time champion Oisin Murphy, 31, to become the youngest winner since Charlie Elliott in 1923. “Nearly four years ago when I was going up to Newcastle for my first ride, my aim then was just to have a few winners really," Loughnane said on a Great British Racing media call earlier this week. "If anyone had said that day that four years later I’d be where I am now I’d have said they were absolutely crazy." The 20-year-old, who has recorded more than 220 victories this year, will now turn his sights to Gordon Richards' 1947 record of 269 winners in a calendar year.

Source: Reuters

STRASBOURG, France, Oct 17 : Paris St Germain coach Luis Enrique gambled with a much-changed starting lineup and was almost made to pay as the Ligue 1 champions rode their luck to claim a 3-1 victory at RC Strasbourg on Saturday. Gio Reyna put the home side ahead in the first half and they might have added to that tally but for the brilliance of PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov. Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty for the visitors in the second half but minutes later they were level through Ilya Zabarnyi before Dembele scored five minutes from the end of the 90 and Desire Doue netted a third in added time. The win moves PSG top of the table on goals scored with 14 points from seven games, ahead of Lille, who drew 1-1 at home to Brest, and AS Monaco before they visit Lorient on Sunday.

Luis Enrique made eight changes to his team from the midweek Champions League win at Manchester City with only Safonov, Warren Zaïre-Emery and Maghnes Akliouche selected again. Safonov was superb as he thwarted Strasbourg several times before PSG earned the points late on. They finished the game with 10 men as defender Nuno Mendes was withdrawn with no substitutions remaining. "He felt a little thing (on his thigh) and we decided to play with one less player so as not to take risks," Luis Enrique told reporters. DEMBELE PENALTY MISS Dembele missed a second-half penalty with the score at 1-0 to Strasbourg, but put that disappointment behind him to net one goal, assist another and play a part in the third. "I told him if you play 25 minutes and give an assist and score a goal, you don't need to play more. That's enough," Luis Enrique said. Dembele's penalty miss meant PSG have scored one of their four spot-kicks this season, a poor record from 12 yards. "He was angry because he missed the penalty. It's true, we have a statistic (from penalties) that is a little difficult to take," Luis Enrique added. "We have many players who can shoot but it is true that we lack a specialist (penalty-taker)." Lille were held by Brest as 40-year-old Olivier Giroud equalised for the hosts from the penalty spot after 64 minutes. Brest took an early lead through Mama Balde and climb to eighth on nine points. Lens rose to seventh on 10 points after a 3-1 win at second-bottom Troyes. They took the lead through an Adrien Monfray own goal after 13 minutes before Odsonne Edouard and Ruben Aguilar secured the points after Timothe Nkada equalised for the hosts.

Source: Reuters

Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday (Oct 17), including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said. The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since Oct 6, the ministry said in a statement. The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community . The three health workers, two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively, managed the index case on Oct 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since Oct 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed.

The second and third patients confirmed earlier are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5 percent, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85 percent global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission. Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, the second-largest outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.

Commentary: This Ebola outbreak should never have caught the world off guard

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The first Kenyan case was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on Oct 3. He died on Oct 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

Source: Reuters/fs

A crush at a religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed at least 17 people and injured dozens, local media reported on Saturday (Oct 11). Durga Puja, a multi-day annual Hindu festival in the state of West Bengal, draws huge crowds to temporary structures known as pandals that house idols of the goddess Durga. The incident occurred at the exit gate in Kolkata's Girish Park area after heavy rain led to overcrowding as large numbers of devotees attempted to leave the venue, local TV said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office, in a post on social media platform X, announced a compensation payment of 200,000 rupees (US$2,106.15) for the next of kin of those who died and 50,000 rupees each for the injured.

SEVILLE, Spain, Oct 17 : Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals. Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentin Gomez and Ez Abde replied for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for headbutting Lamine. Barca moved to 27 points, five above Atletico who won 1-0 at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis have 19 and Real Madrid sit fourth on 18 before welcoming Sevilla on Sunday, Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini made eight changes from the side that beat Porto 3-2 in the Champions League, resting several key players including Antony, Marc Bartra, Natan and Isco with a midweek European meeting against Feyenoord in mind.

Yet the hosts still made Barca sweat before the visitors eventually found space, rhythm and, after Betis were reduced to 10 men, plenty of room to turn the match into another attacking exhibition. Lamine opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gomez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Barcelona reclaimed the lead in the 41st minute when Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermin Lopez's corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso's spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho Hernandez was adjudged to have handled earlier in the build-up. Jesus, signed from Arsenal in the close season, had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly inside the area. A minute later Abde pulled one back on the counter, sliding a low shot inside the right post, but Betis' celebrations turned sour when Bernal was shown a straight red card following a scuffle. Lamine was booked for his part in the altercation. Barcelona made it 4-2 in the 63rd minute when Alvaro Valles failed to deal with Lamine's free kick and Pau Cubarsi headed the loose ball back across goal for Garcia to tap in. Olmo completed the rout in the 81st minute, curling a right-footed shot into the top corner from outside the box. Atletico won 1-0 at Espanyol, with Baena coming off the bench to deliver the late sting in a cagey match in Barcelona. Both sides struck the post in a tight tactical contest before Atletico's substitutes combined in the 89th, Julian Alvarez bursting down the left and squaring for Baena, who drove a fierce strike into the top corner from the edge of the box.

Source: Reuters

PARIS: Rioting erupted in cities across France on Saturday (Oct 17) as demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled out of control in some of the worst violence the country has witnessed for decades. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers. In Limoges the city hall was set ablaze, in Marseille black-clad protesters broke into City Hall and defaced the building with anarchic graffiti and in Lyon protesters torched the city's tourist office. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "far-left" and criminals just months before a presidential election next year.

"To those who clearly want to use this violence as a 'warm-up' before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence," he wrote in a post on X. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters that about 400 people had been arrested after violent incidents, most of whom were adults. Around 550,000 people had participated in the demonstrations across the country, he said. The CGT union told Reuters it estimated protesters at 800,000 people. President Emmanuel Macron vowed to prosecute and punish people who had performed such attacks.

Teenager shoots headmaster, teacher at French school

France students plan more protests, UN 'concerned' over violence

France pledges more teachers after school students vow no let-up

"We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who only seek to undermine our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so," he wrote in a post on X. Belgium, Portugal and Italy also faced smaller-scale protests on Saturday as living costs rise in Europe, while protesters in Albania again rallied against perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards. Protesters said most people had marched peacefully, and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police. Many held signs bearing slogans against the police, the president and the wealthy. "We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said Lola, a 19-year-old protester in Paris. TEAR GAS, FIRE AND LOOTING Most protests kicked off around midday , with some beginning before the official start of the demonstrations. In some parts of Paris, police fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas. Rioters tried to break into the Galeries Lafayette department store, smashed up banks, ransacked a Lacoste store as well as other boutiques and looted an SFR mobile phone shop. Protesters had been setting objects ablaze all day, including numerous cars.

A Centaure, a multi-purpose intervention armoured vehicle of the French Gendarmerie Nationale, is seen in street amid clashes between protesters and the French riot police during a demonstration against the cost of living and rising fuel prices in Marseille, as part of nationwide protests called by the "Yellow Vests" movement, joined by French high school and university students, teachers and parents demanding better school conditions and government action, as well as labour unions, workers, farmers and retirees. Oct 17, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Manon Cruz)

In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people protested in Brussels, and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. In Albania , police fired what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down. In Portugal, tens of thousands took to the streets of Lisbon following days of unrest to protest against housing and other living costs. Housing prices in Portugal have doubled since 2017, fuelling one of the worst affordability crises in Europe. In Italy, a march against high costs of living in Milan degenerated into disorder, with police clearing the central Cathedral square with tear gas. Police in Bologna used water cannon to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after another protest turned violent, the ANSA news agency reported. FRENCH POLICE RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY The protests in France began last month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards. In Paris on Saturday, protesters in high-visibility vests blocked streets, recalling the Yellow Vest movement that marked President Emmanuel Macron's previous term in office. Saturday's protests eclipsed the size of the crowds at the peak of the Yellow Vest movement, though they were far lower than the levels seen at the protests in 2023 against Macron's pension overhaul.

Protesters throw rocks at police during an anti-government demonstration outside the Education Ministry, in Tirana, Albania, Oct 17, 2026. (Photo: AP/Hameraldi Agolli)

Macron is entering the final stretch of his presidency, facing a fragmented political landscape and growing pressure over the economy. France's efforts to reduce public debt have failed to reassure investors, pushing government borrowing costs to their highest levels in over two decades. Police tactics have drawn criticism following injuries among demonstrators, including a teenager who lost a hand after picking up a stun grenade. The police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen allegations of police violence. Lecornu said more than 900 police officers had also been injured in previous protests. Nunez said one person lost his hand in clashes with police on Saturday. French media reported he tried to pick up a stun grenade. The UNSA police union posted a video on X showing crowds attacking police vans with clubs and bricks in multiple locations. The union warned the government police forces were at breaking point. “Today again, in every corner of France, our colleagues are being used as punching bags. Pelted with stones, injured, trapped in real ambushes,” the union said. “Let everyone take responsibility: this cannot go on indefinitely. The rope is stretched to its maximum."

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 17 : Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club. City are appealing a ruling that they breached 114 Premier League financial rules and deny wrongdoing, but the uncertainty off the pitch has done little to disrupt them on it. Enzo Maresca's side have won seven league games from seven for their best-ever start to a Premier League season. Maresca became the first manager to win his opening seven Premier League games in charge as City bounced back from Wednesday's Champions League defeat by Paris St Germain, his first meaningful loss as City boss. Haaland struck twice after Phil Foden's first goal of the season had been cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, with the Norwegian's second his 100th non-penalty Premier League goal, reached in a record 139 appearances.

He was denied a hat-trick by an offside in the build-up before Zian Flemming's stoppage-time penalty made the scoreline closer than the game felt. But victory came at a potentially heavy cost during a punishing stretch of four games in 10 days. While Maresca had made six changes to his team from Wednesday, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly all went off injured, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "Unfortunately, in 10 minutes, we had four, five players (hurt)," Maresca said. "I don't have any news at the moment." Haaland made a beeline for the tunnel rather than staying to applaud supporters, unusual for the striker, with Semenyo hobbling off not far behind. DEFIANT VOICE "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." The uncertainty surrounding City has hardly dampened the mood among their supporters, who were in defiant voice at the Etihad as a stadium-record 60,817 watched the game. They loudly booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off and waved inflatable bananas, reviving a City tradition dating from their days outside the top flight in the 1980s. Supporters turned the prospect of possible relegation as a sanction into gallows humour, chanting "You're going down with the City!" at the travelling Ipswich fans. Outside the stadium, vendors did brisk business selling bananas and T-shirts carrying anti-charge slogans, including "Stick your charges where the sun don't shine" and "City til I die." "The environment was very good," Maresca said. "They just said to me that today was a record attendance, so that's also a nice thing. The fans, the club, the players, we are all together in this journey, and this is the best feeling for everyone." Maresca has said several times since the team reconvened after the international break that he has instructed his players to shut out external criticism as the club appeals the guilty verdict. Captain Ruben Dias said earlier in the week that "it's almost impossible to avoid seeing something, even us being as private as we can be and just doing our own lives on your phone. It's impossible to avoid everything." Maresca praised his players for their focus. "The players, they need to be worried about people inside the club and about me for the credit I give to them, and they are not worried about people that can judge them from outside. "But inside, I promise you that the players they are happy. The club gives credit to the players. I give credit to the players. So this is for us the most important thing." Asked about managing against City with everything that has happened off the pitch, Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil shrugged and said: "No. Just us against City trying to win. Bananas, no bananas, makes no difference."

LONDON, Oct 17 : Liverpool bounced back from last week’s 3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances. Keane Lewis-Potter had given the home side the lead in the 44th minute but Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for an attempted headbutt deep into first-half stoppage time, and Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak completed Liverpool's comeback with second-half goals to seal the three points.  "Super-happy with the win. It's a tough ground, it's a tough team to play, especially away from home. We knew it was going to be a bit of a scrappy game and it's important to come out on top," Isak said.  Vitaly Janelt picked up a second yellow card in stoppage time to leave Brentford with nine men, and Barcola then squandered another opportunity when he opted to pass rather than shoot after Liverpool broke forward on the counter-attack.

BUSINESS AS USUAL FOR CITY Dark clouds remain over the Etihad Stadium with Manchester City's fate still unknown after they appealed a ruling that the club breached 114 Premier League financial rules. City have always denied any wrongdoing. But on the pitch it is very much business as usual, especially for Norwegian goal machine Haaland. Phil Foden gave City a short-lived lead cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, but Haaland restored the home side's advantage before halftime with a header from Mateo Kovacic's cross. The defiant mood was soured somewhat though as Haaland went off with an apparent injury late on, as did Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." FEISTY FIRST HALF Chelsea have had a knack of scoring early this season but were kept at bay by hosts Everton in a feisty and physical first half that produced five yellow cards. However, Xabi Alonso's visitors needed just 43 seconds after the restart to go 1-0 up when Jorrel Hato cut the ball back from the byline to find Neto who swept home. Keeper Martinez's clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite resulted in the Argentine being strapped to a stretcher and taken off, leading to 11 minutes of stoppage time. Chelsea doubled their lead in the 90th minute when Neto pounced on a loose ball after Jordan Henderson's free kick was blocked by the wall, finding the bottom corner with a composed finish as Everton suffered their first defeat of the season. "What we know is he (Martinez) left the stadium conscious and right now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests," Alonso said. "It was concussion but more than that I saw only one clip. Hopefully it won't be too bad but we need to wait." Martinez's knock gave 21-year-old keeper Mike Penders the chance to make his Premier League debut and he helped Chelsea keep a clean sheet in the league for the first time in 23 games. "We need a clean sheet, to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike did as well," Alonso added. BRENTFORD'S YARMOLYUK SENT OFF Liverpool deservedly fell behind at Brentford with Keane Lewis-Potter putting the hosts in front. Brentford were good value for their lead but Yarmolyuk's rush of blood to the head when he clashed with Jeremy Jacquet at a Liverpool corner changed the game. After referee John Brooks was invited to check a VAR monitor he brandished the red card at Ukrainian Yarmolyuk. Liverpool huffed and puffed after the break but Victor Munoz finally levelled in the 62nd minute when he cut in to beat keeper Caoimhin Kelleher with a left-foot finish. Alexander Isak won it for Andoni Iraola's side eight minutes later with a clinical strike from Bradley Barcola's assist. Brentford ended with nine men after Vitaly Janelt got a second yellow card for a foul on substitute Rio Ngumoha. Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute strike for Fulham was enough to earn their new manager Alvaro Arbeloa a long-overdue league win and move Fulham up to 16th. Johan Manzambi's early goal secured Villa's victory at Newcastle, their second of the season.

Source: Reuters

NEW DELHI: India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday (Oct 17), a day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning. CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the terms. Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday. "Please, spare the people of India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

Related:

STUDENT GROUPS CALL FOR MORE PROTEST ACTION Dipke was detained on Friday as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban. Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday. The movement, which was mobilised by the youth and joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

Source: Reuters/dy
